title: Claims proposed for one target (a dataset and one of its papers)
description: Draft. To be revised after the pilot.

dataset.description: The dataset the claims are tested on: the archive and the dataset's identifier there.

archive.description: The archive that holds the dataset, in lower case: dandi, ebrains, openneuro, dryad, zenodo, figshare and so on.

id.description: The dataset's identifier in that archive, e.g. 000003 on DANDI.

doi.description: The dataset's DOI, when it has one: an identifier that holds across archives.

id.description: Stable within the file, e.g. fig2b.

statement.description: The finding in one or two sentences, in words. Not a copy of the figure.

source.description: Where the paper shows it, precise enough to find without searching: a figure panel, e.g. 'Figure 2B', or a section and paragraph, e.g. 'Results, Place fields, paragraph 3'.

kind.description: A finding the paper reports (`finding`, the default), or a check the registry adds that the dataset is the data the paper's outside material describes (`link`: the paper's tables, source data, code or deposits). Links are not findings of the paper and are counted apart from them.

quote.description: The sentence of the paper that states the finding, word for word, from the place `source` names, so a reader can check the statement against the paper. Cut with '...' where it runs long. From the full text.

inferred.description: For a finding with no quote: why the statement is the author's reading and not a sentence of the paper, e.g. 'Numbers from Supplementary Table 1; no sentence states them.'

expected.description: The reported numbers the claim rests on, each with a tolerance: one, or a list.

statistics.description: The statistical support the paper reports for the finding: one entry per test or interval, as the paper gives it. A record of the paper, not a target with a tolerance (that is `expected`).

criterion.description: For a claim without a number, how it will be judged. Written before the analysis is run.

depends_on.description: Ids of claims in this file whose result this one uses.

data.description: What the claim's test uses: the dataset alone (`dataset`, the default); the dataset with names for its own codes taken from elsewhere (`with_labels`), which counts as the dataset; the dataset with other data from elsewhere (`with_inputs`), which is counted apart; or data the paper deposited in another public archive, which the dataset does not hold (`elsewhere`), counted apart from both. Outside sources that a test uses are listed under `inputs` in the attempt.

where.description: For a claim with data `elsewhere`: the archive and the pinned identifier of the data, e.g. 'PRIDE PXD012345' or 'Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.123'.

checks.description: Checks of the claims file against the paper by a second reader (docs/protocol.md, Reader, step 5), oldest first. The file is ready for an attempt when the last says so.

about.description: What the test compares or the interval bounds, when the claim has more than one, e.g. 'GPi against VLa onset times'.

test.description: The test as the paper names it, e.g. 'Wilcoxon rank-sum', 'two-tailed t-test'.

statistic.description: The test statistic as reported, e.g. 't(14) = 3.2', 'F(2, 40) = 5.1', 'r = 0.38'.

p.description: The reported p-value as printed, or its bound when the paper gives one ('p < 0.05' is p 0.05 with p_relation '<'). A paper that prints 'P = 0' (below the precision it reports) is recorded as 0.

p_relation.description: How p was reported: exactly (the default) or as a bound.

corrected.description: The correction for multiple comparisons the paper applied, e.g. 'Bonferroni', 'FDR'.

n.description: The sample the test was run on, in words, e.g. '206 GPi and 179 VLa units'.
